blocks.content: NITI Aayog serves as the premier policy Think Tank of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs while fostering cooperative federalism.

rows: Empowered to allocate funds to ministries and state governments
Advisory body only; fund allocation power lies with Finance Ministry
Limited engagement through National Development Council
Direct participation in Governing Council (CMs & Lt. Governors)

items: NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created via an executive Cabinet resolution, not by an Act of Parliament.
The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson, while the Governing Council comprises all State Chief Ministers and Lt. Governors of UTs.
Unlike the former Planning Commission, NITI Aayog has no power to allocate financial funds to state governments or central ministries.
The SDG India Index score ranges between 0 and 100, categorizing entities into Achiever (100), Front Runner (65-99), Performer (50-64), and Aspirant (0-49).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the 65-year-old Planning Commission on January 1, 2015, shifting from a top-down to a bottom-up policy approach.
The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) launched in 2018 focuses on rapidly transforming 112 of India's most developmentally challenged districts based on 49 Key Performance Indicators.
Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) promotes innovation and entrepreneurship by establishing Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) in schools and Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) for startups.
The SDG India Index comprehensively tracks and ranks the progress of all States and Union Territories toward achieving the United Nations 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
Project SATH (Sustainable Action for Transforming Human Capital) aims to initiate systemic transformation in Education (SATH-E) and Health (SATH-H) across partner states.
